records.name: Vern L. Lindquist
records.notes: Named JCC's fourth president; announced Dec 16, 2022, began role Jan 16, 2023, after a search that considered five finalists.

records.name: Kenneth Boham
records.notes: Served as interim president in 2022 following Dr. David Johnson's departure and before Lindquist's arrival.

records.name: David N. Johnson
records.notes: JCC's third president, selected after Dr. Reichard (second president) retired in June 2009. Founding president was John L. Tart (1969-1998).

records.name: Susan D. Looney
records.priorTitle: Senior Vice President of Academic Affairs/Provost
records.notes: Became RACC's sixth president on July 1, 2018, after rising internally from Dean of Instruction (2014) to Provost (2015). Earlier career included Mohave Community College, Delaware Technical Community College, and Colorado Mountain College.

records.name: Unknown (fifth president)
records.notes: RACC's site confirms Looney is the sixth president, implying five predecessors, but does not name the immediate (fifth) predecessor. An earlier president referenced in older records is Dr. Richard A. Kratz, though his exact tenure years could not be confirmed.

records.name: William P. Mullaney
records.notes: Became RCC's ninth president in June 2025, focusing on strategic partnerships and academic program expansion.

records.name: Lester Edgardo Sandres Rápalo
records.notes: Became the eighth president in 2023 (approved by SUNY June 6, took office July 1) but parted ways with the college the same year after a substantial budget deficit was uncovered. Beth A. Coyle then served as Officer in Charge (2023-2024) before Mullaney's arrival.

records.name: Michael A. Baston
records.notes: Seventh president, 2017-2022; succeeded by Susan Deer as Officer in Charge (2022-2023). Preceded by Clifford L. Wood (2004-2017).

records.name: Tony D. Hawkins
records.notes: Eighth president of SUNY Broome; took office July 1, 2023, succeeding longtime president Kevin Drumm.

records.name: Kevin Drumm
records.notes: Served roughly 13 years as SUNY Broome president (approx. 2009-2023) before retiring; announced retirement May 2022, departed July 2023. Founding president of the institution (1947) was Cecil C. Tyrrell; the intervening chain of six presidents between Tyrrell and Drumm was not confirmed.

records.name: Fernando Figueroa
records.notes: Started as Gateway's second President/CEO on July 1, 2016. Effective July 1, 2026, his title changed from President to Chancellor system-wide across KCTCS colleges under HB 619/KCTCS reforms (the title 'President' is now reserved for the statewide KCTCS system leader). Duties/responsibilities are unchanged, only the title.

records.name: G. Edward Hughes
records.notes: Founding President/CEO from December 1, 2001; retired in September 2015 amid board criticism over declining enrollment, ahead of Figueroa's July 2016 start.

seats.university: West Kentucky Community and Technical College

records.name: Anton Reece
records.priorTitle: Vice President/administrator at WKCTC (formerly Paducah Community College)
records.priorInstitution: West Kentucky Community and Technical College
records.notes: Became WKCTC's second president on October 1, 2016, having joined the college in 1990 as a minority affairs coordinator/counselor. As of July 2026, KCTCS system-wide reforms (HB 619) renamed college-level 'President' titles to 'Chancellor,' reserving 'President' for the statewide KCTCS system leader; Reece's exact title-change date at WKCTC was not separately confirmed but Gateway CTC's equivalent change was effective July 1, 2026.

records.name: Barbara Veazey
records.notes: Inaugurated as WKCTC's first president in 2003, following the 2003 merger of Paducah Community College and West Kentucky Technical College.

records.name: Christy (Christina) Ponce
records.notes: Became Temple College president in January 2019. Also worked previously at El Paso Community College and Austin Community College; named to the inaugural Aspen Presidential Fellowship for Community College Excellence (2016) and Aspen New Presidents Fellowship (2021). Her immediate predecessor at Temple College could not be confirmed from available sources.

records.name: Jean Runyon
records.notes: Hired as PVCC president, announced April 21, 2022. PVCC's official website was unreachable (persistent 503 errors) during research, and her predecessor's name could not be independently confirmed from available secondary sources.

records.name: Lisa Avery
records.notes: Began as LBCC president July 1, 2020, following a nationwide search; had led PCC's Sylvania campus (largest PCC campus, ~27,000 students) since 2015.

records.name: Greg Hamann
records.notes: Served approximately ten years as LBCC president (c. 2010-2020) before retiring.

records.name: Keith Curry
records.priorInstitution: Compton Community College Center (during El Camino College partnership)
records.notes: Led the college's rebuilding effort as provost during its partnership with El Camino College, becoming President/CEO around 2016 and overseeing restoration of full independent accreditation on June 7, 2017. Exact presidency start date is approximate; not precisely dated in available sources.

records.name: Doris P. Givens / Lawrence M. Cox
records.notes: Givens (2006-2008) and Cox (2008-2010) served consecutively as Provost/CEO after Compton lost independent accreditation and partnered with El Camino College following the 2004-2006 accreditation crisis (during which Rita Cepeda and Jamillah Moore served as interim presidents in 2005).

seats.university: Rowan College of South Jersey-Gloucester Campus

records.name: Brenden Rickards
records.priorTitle: Vice President and Provost of Academic Services
records.notes: Joined RCSJ in 2007 as a biology professor; named interim president July 1, 2025, following Frederick Keating's retirement, and made permanent president January 20, 2026.

records.name: Frederick Keating
records.priorInstitution: Rowan College of South Jersey (Gloucester campus, predecessor institution)
records.notes: President of the Gloucester campus institution from February 2012, continuing as president of the merged Rowan College of South Jersey after the 2019 merger with the Cumberland campus, through his retirement in summer 2025.

records.name: Russell A. Davis
records.notes: Served September 2008-April 13, 2011, resigned and was later charged with forgery counts.

records.name: Todd Haynie
records.notes: Current president of Eastern Arizona College, succeeding Mark Smith Bryce in 2018. Exact start month and prior role were not confirmed from available sources.

records.name: Mark Smith Bryce
records.notes: Oversaw construction of the middle campus, Nursing Education building, and Alumni Visitors Center during his 2002-2018 tenure.

records.name: Gherald L. Hoopes Jr.
records.notes: Led initiatives including launching the Cosmetology Program and achieving financial stability through equalization funding.

records.name: Monica Brown
records.notes: Selected as South Seattle College president through Seattle Colleges' 2024 presidential search (which simultaneously searched for leaders of all three Seattle Colleges campuses). Start date is approximate (2024); her immediate predecessor and prior role could not be confirmed from available sources -- the South Seattle College campus president reports to the Seattle Colleges district Chancellor.

records.name: Jeffery S. Boyd
records.priorTitle: Unknown (prior experience at Tidewater CC and Elgin CC)
records.priorInstitution: Tidewater Community College (VA) / Elgin Community College (IL)
records.notes: Serving as RCTC president since July 1, 2018. Holds a doctorate in Community College Leadership.

records.name: Mary Davenport / Joyce Helens
records.notes: Served as consecutive interim presidents between McClellon's departure (2016) and Boyd's arrival (2018).

records.name: Leslie R. McClellon
records.notes: Preceded by interim Gail C. O'Kane (2013-2014) and permanent president Donald D. Supalla (1997-2013, also interim 1997-2000).

records.name: Deidra Peaslee
records.notes: Became Saint Paul College's first female president in March 2021, two years after Rassoul Dastmozd's resignation; the interim leadership between 2019 and 2021 was not confirmed.

records.name: Rassoul Dastmozd
records.notes: Resigned effective June 30, 2019, following an accreditation review site visit that documented faculty reports describing a leadership climate of 'fear and intimidation.'

records.name: John B. Buxton
records.notes: Named president in June 2020, taking office July 2020.

records.name: Bill Ingram
records.notes: Served January 2008-June 2020.

records.name: Phail Wynn Jr.
records.notes: Long-serving president, November 1980-December 2007; later became a senior Duke University administrator. Founding leaders were Harold K. Collins (1961-1975) and John Crumpton (1975-1980).

records.name: Hope E. Rivers
records.notes: Selected by the PTC Area Commission in November 2020 following a nationwide search; became effective president January 4, 2021 -- the college's third president, and its first woman and first person of color to hold the role. Her immediate predecessor ('longtime president') was not named in available sources.

records.name: Jay Allen
records.priorTitle: Unknown (came from Hopkinsville Community College, KY)
records.notes: Became ICC's seventh president on July 1, 2017. His immediate (sixth) predecessor could not be confirmed from available sources.
